[b]Montfleur: La Patrïe et li Communistes[/b]

The sudden rise of Communism in various states across Erene, and the seeming sudden rise of the nation known as Qianxan had unsettled the austere and highly liberal monarchy of Montfleur. Montfleur had dealt with communism before, the very institution of Li Comunes dEstat as a government subdivision had been as a result of communard reforms done in the late 19th century under king Robert DEstienne. However, this brand of communism, known as the ideology of Cui Fang among other names, would draw concern, from even the Communist Party of Montfleur. 

Communism in Montfleur had not arrived through revolution, but through intellectualism, the rise of Montfleur in the 18th and 19th centuries as a minor power in geopolitics had permitted it to become a bastion for free thought, as such Communism had never taken the revolutionary tint of perhaps its originators. Communism in Montfleur is best described as that of a more intellectual variety, where revolution is ultimately attained through the progression of ideals towards a communist state, wherein the bourgeois are gradually subsumed by the progression of society and technology to a point where they become obsolete. The chief founder of this ideology was that of Dr. Jean Luc Baptise, a 19th century sociologist and professor who had partaken in the 1st commune of 1857 with the students of La Escole Nacionel de Montfleur against the policies of the 1st duke of Belgarde which sought to crack down on the liberal leaning reforms of the monarchy under king Louis-Phillipe IV. Thus Communism as accepted in Montfleur was more polite and cooperation driven, with the ideal being Coperéz jusques que lobsoletiun viengne, alors li pueples se levera. 

Thus the sudden rise of revolutionary communism once more, and the formation of the internationale brought swift condemnation from the Communist Party of Montfleur (Also known as Li Baptistes). With the head of the party coming out stating that Revolutionary Communism is not what is needed among the civilised nations of Erene, we are past the days of bloody and violent struggle, we must work to bend the will of the bourgeois to the people through cooperation and mutual acceptance of the fact that all people are by nature equal in their creation, having the same rights as endowed by their creator, whether king or common-worker.

In the meantime the monarchy of Montfleur itself had turned its eyes towards the seemingly odd Holy Orthodox Empire that had arisen to its south, with King Henri XVII lamenting that the once forward thinking and liberal state had devolved into feudal hierarchism and pietistic posturing.
